Modern.brandNameRationale: Reefline is modern reef-keeping shorthand — the term hobbyists use for the visible band of coral across a tank. Single compound word, app-ready, works for retail and software.
Modern.industrySummary: Modern reef-keeping has moved from forums to mobile-first communities. The opening is for a brand that takes the Berlin-method tradition and presents it with the discipline of a software product — clean nomenclature, structured logs, app-readable.
Modern.competitorLandscape: Bulk Reef Supply (bulkreefsupply.com) holds the modern reef-supply slot. Tropical Marine Centre (tropicalmarinecentre.co.uk) plays the UK trade peer. Red Sea (redsea.com) is the modern system reference. We sit alongside Red Sea, with a sharper app-first identity.
Modern.positioningStatement: A modern reef-keeping brand for hobbyists who track their tanks like software.

targetAudience.primary: 28 to 45. Keeps a 90 to 200 gallon reef. Logs parameters weekly. Has a wavemaker schedule on their phone.
behaviors: Buys frags from named coral farms
Reads forum threads on Berlin-method dosing

dos: Treat the app like the brand

Modern.logoDirection: A wordmark only. Reefline set in a precise grotesk, with a thin horizontal rule cutting across the baseline — the reefline itself. Used as the app icon at small scale.

colorPalette.name: Reef Blue
colorPalette.meaning: Deep water at the reef edge.

typography.primary: Söhne for the wordmark and product UI
typography.rationale: One typeface family. Mono for the numbers, regular for the brand. Two voices, one app.

Luxury.tagline: Marine biology in the Naples tradition.
Luxury.brandNameRationale: Direct echo of the Stazione Zoologica Anton Dohrn in Naples, founded 1872 — the world's oldest marine research station. Italian phrasing, scholarly luxury register. The name does not claim institutional lineage; it places the brand in the same intellectual tradition.
Luxury.industrySummary: Luxury aquariums are dominated by hotel installations and private commissions. The opening is for an Italian-coded marine atelier with the scholarly authority of a research station — bespoke marine tanks for residences, yachts, and institutions.
Luxury.competitorLandscape: Aquarium Architecture (aquariumarchitecture.com) is the UK luxury installation reference. Living Color (livingcolor.com) holds the institutional aquarium peer. Reynolds Polymer (reynoldspolymer.com) plays the high-end acrylic specialist slot. We sit smaller and more scholarly, with Italian marine-station heritage.
Luxury.positioningStatement: A scholarly marine atelier in the Naples research-station tradition, building bespoke saltwater installations.

targetAudience.primary: 50 to 75. Owns a coastal home or yacht. Commissions one marine installation a decade. Reads scientific monographs on Mediterranean species.
behaviors: Commissions a private marine biologist for stocking advice
Travels to Naples and Monaco oceanographic museums
Pays a premium for documented species provenance

donts: Photograph the tank with cinematic filters

Luxury.logoDirection: A serif wordmark — Stazione Marina set in a classical Italian roman with a small engraved sea-anemone mark. Used on the commission certificate and the brass tank plate.

colorPalette.name: Naples Blue
colorPalette.meaning: The Bay of Naples at depth.

typography.secondary: Adobe Garamond for monographs and commission letters
typography.rationale: Sectra carries the scholarly register. Garamond keeps long-form scientific copy warm.

Minimal.tagline: Where the water meets the air.
Minimal.brandNameRationale: Two syllables — salinity and waterline. Saltline names the visible band at the top of every marine tank. Single compound word, period-locked register, minimal aquarium brand.
Minimal.industrySummary: Minimal in the aquarium category is rare — the trade leans toward reef-stunt imagery. The opening is for a brand that strips the visual language back to the tank itself: glass, water, salt.
Minimal.competitorLandscape: BiOrb (biorb.com) holds the design-led minimal slot. Waterbox (waterboxaquariums.com) plays the modern rimless peer. ADA (adana.co.jp) is the minimal aquascape reference. We sit alongside ADA with marine instead of freshwater focus.
Minimal.positioningStatement: A minimal saltwater brand for tanks that look like furniture.

targetAudience.primary: 30 to 55. Lives in a small considered home. Wants one rimless tank in the living room and nothing extra.
behaviors: Buys a single rimless cube tank

donts: Photograph the tank with branded backgrounds

Minimal.logoDirection: Saltline set in a neutral grotesque, all lowercase, with a single thin rule beneath — the salt line itself. No icon.

typography.primary: ABC Diatype for the wordmark and body
typography.secondary: ABC Diatype Mono for parameter chips
typography.rationale: One family. Mono for the numbers.

Corporate.tagline: Life-support and filtration for marine installations.
Corporate.brandNameRationale: Marinex pairs marine with the -ex industrial suffix used across life-support and engineering trades. Systems names the actual product: integrated life-support architecture for public aquariums, research institutions, and large private installations.
Corporate.industrySummary: Corporate aquariums is a serious B2B category — life-support systems for public aquariums, research institutions, and aquaculture. The opening is for a mid-tier life-support specialist with documented system engineering.
Corporate.competitorLandscape: Aquatic Life Support Systems (aquaticlifesupport.com) holds the public-aquarium engineering slot. Pentair Aquatic Eco-Systems (pentairaes.com) plays the global supplier peer. Sea & Reef Aquaculture (seareef.com) sits in the aquaculture peer slot. We sit alongside Pentair AES with a sharper system-integration identity.
Corporate.positioningStatement: Corporate life-support and filtration engineering for marine installations over 1,000 gallons.

targetAudience.primary: Public aquarium operations managers, research-institution facility leads, and aquaculture procurement officers.
behaviors: Renews on five to ten-year terms

dos: Lead with system capacity and uptime
Speak the language of facility engineers

Corporate.logoDirection: A wordmark — MARINEX in a tight engineering grotesk above SYSTEMS in tracked small caps. A single hexagonal water-flow mark sits beside the wordmark on technical documents.

typography.primary: Inter for marketing and B2B documents
typography.secondary: Source Serif Pro for printed engineering reports
typography.rationale: Inter scales clean across digital. The serif handles printed technical documentation.

Creative.brandNameRationale: The Glass Reef is editorial phrasing — the reef contained behind glass. Reads as a creative aquascaping studio that treats each tank as a gallery installation rather than equipment.
Creative.industrySummary: Creative aquariums is dominated by hobbyist content. The opening is for an aquascaping studio with a gallery posture — bespoke planted and marine tanks photographed and exhibited like installations.
Creative.competitorLandscape: Green Aqua (greenaqua.hu) holds the aquascape gallery peer slot. Aquarium Design Group (aquariumdesigngroup.com) plays the US bespoke peer. The Aquarium Co-Op (aquariumcoop.com) is the community-creative reference. We sit closer to Aquarium Design Group with an editorial gallery identity.
Creative.positioningStatement: A creative aquascaping studio building tanks as gallery installations.

targetAudience.primary: 35 to 60. Collects design objects. Treats the home tank as a piece of art, not equipment.
behaviors: Commissions the tank like an installation
Buys plants and corals from named cultivators

dos: Photograph the tank as an installation
Name the cultivator and the species
Treat each commission as a one-off

Creative.logoDirection: A wordmark — The Glass Reef in a calm editorial serif with a thin reef-silhouette rule beneath. The rule appears on the gallery catalogue and the commission certificate.

typography.primary: GT Sectra for the wordmark and catalogue
typography.secondary: PP Mori for body and captions
typography.rationale: Sectra makes the catalogue feel like a small art journal. Mori keeps the captions calm.
